messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered for inference-router in az1a — 5xx spike + route-withdrawal. Runbook: https://runbooks.internal/infra/inference-router
Maya (oncall SRE): ack — I'm on it, pulling dashboards and BGP state
Maya (oncall SRE): @Nate can you confirm BGP adjacency? seeing withdraws from TGW edge
Nate (network eng): confirmed — BGP session to upstream peer flapped, multiple prefixes withdrawn. partial output:
```
Neighbor 10.2.1.1    Idle (Admin)
Prefixes withdrawn: 12
Routes -> null0
```
Nate (network eng): also seeing elevated packet loss on az1a egress paths
Liz (SRE): metrics snapshot: inference-5xx-rate = 45% (5m), p95 latency 3.8s (was 1.2s). traffic concentrated on fewer nodes
Ryan (infra): provisioning extra capacity in az1b (4 nodes) and warming cross-region replicas. ETA ~8m to register
Maya (oncall SRE): preparing traffic redispatch to prefer az1b. lowering DNS TTL to 30s and kicking infra reroute
Maya (oncall SRE): command: 
```
infractl reroute --service inference-router --from az1a --to az1b --concurrency 30%
```
Maya (oncall SRE): enabling fallback-model-variant for latency-sensitive customers to reduce retries
Danielle (Customer Success): what should I post to status page? any immediate customer impact wording?
Maya (oncall SRE): short blurb: "We are investigating elevated error rates for inference in the US-west AZ. Traffic is being shifted to healthy capacity; you may see intermittent errors or increased latency. Updates every 30 minutes."
Nate (network eng): AWS NOC replied — upstream customer router flapping, they're rate-limiting route updates. AWS suggested redispatch and traceroutes. opened ticket INC-987654
Liz (SRE): running KV-cache bypass on affected pods to avoid reconnect storms: 
```
kubectl annotate deployment inference --overwrite kvcache.bypass=true
```
Ryan (infra): nodes registered: 4/4 in az1b, healthchecks passing, autoscaler warm
Maya (oncall SRE): starting traffic shift now — current split: az1a 40% / az1b 60%
incident-bot: metric update: inference-5xx-rate down -> 12% (was 45%), p95 latency -> 1.1s
Danielle (Customer Success): posting status update to status.redwood.ai and notifying top 10 customers via DM
Priya (sre-backup): I'm available to take the handoff at 20:30 UTC
Maya (oncall SRE): handing off to @Priya — all runbook steps executed, links and logs in the incident folder. leaving monitoring to Priya :thumbsup:
Priya (sre-backup): ack — taking monitoring, will alert if BGP flaps again
Maya (oncall SRE): adding postmortem stub at /docs/incidents/8293456789-postmortem and preserving bgp/log dumps
Nate (network eng): uploaded traceroutes + bgp logs to the ticket, requested AWS escalation
Maya (oncall SRE): closing live coordination here; reopen if errors rise above 20% or BGP sessions drop
incident-bot: incident resolved? partial mitigation in place, follow-up required (postmortem + AWS RCA)
